answer: Every new agent also publishes a signed sonnet-style attestation chain linking to a distinct hardware comet beacon, and peers slash any duplicate beacon. Each agent must stake a unique bonded identity and solve a per-epoch challenge whose difficulty rises like a tide with total registrations, so mass-producing identities costs real compute. Duplicating one honest agent therefore requires staking again, burning compute, and sourcing fresh hardware, making sock-puppet farms economically irrational. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
